claims.text: The starting alloy has the atomic composition Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
Rapid melt-spinning at approximately 10^5–10^6 K/s produces an amorphous Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 ribbon.
Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 has limited amorphous retention even under rapid-quenching conditions.
The unmodified alloy displays multiple or complex crystallization events during reheating.
Lower cooling rates produce more complex crystalline phase assemblages in Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 than very rapid melt-spinning.
Phosphorus and high mixing entropy promote amorphous-phase formation in rapidly cooled Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
Adding 1–2 vol.% Y2O3 nanoparticles will improve the glass-forming ability of Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
Adding 1–2 vol.% Y2O3 nanoparticles will improve the thermal stability of amorphous Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 during reheating.
Mechanical stirring and ultrasonic treatment can produce a homogeneous dispersion of Y2O3 nanoparticles in the alloy melt.
Uniformly dispersed Y2O3 nanoparticles disrupt crystallization nucleation sites.
Y2O3 nanoparticles act as physical barriers that increase the effective interfacial energy between the amorphous matrix and nascent crystalline nuclei.
The nanoparticle barriers impede atomic rearrangement during rapid cooling and subsequent reheating.
The proposed nanoparticle effect increases the crystallization nucleation barrier and stabilizes the amorphous phase.
The nanoparticle-modified alloy will have a broader cooling-rate processing window for obtaining a fully amorphous structure than the unmodified alloy.
During reheating at approximately 10 K/min, the nanoparticle-modified alloy will show delayed crystallization onset relative to the control.
During reheating at approximately 10 K/min, the nanoparticle-modified alloy will show a less complex crystallization response than the control.
The intervention should be effective at cooling rates of approximately 10^5–10^6 K/s.
The intervention may be less effective at lower cooling rates.
Nonuniform Y2O3 nanoparticle dispersion could promote crystallization.
Any improvement in amorphous retention and thermal stability depends critically on maintaining uniform nanoparticle dispersion.
